title: CRLA/202/2013 of Aseem Mallik Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No.202 of 2013
Aseem Mallik S/o Shri Amar Mallik .....Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand .... Respondent
Mr. S.R.S. Gill, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. S.S. Adhikari, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
 Although today only bail application No. 574 of
2013 was listed for disposal, however, in view of the fact
that lower court record has already been received, Mr.
S.R.S. Gill, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr.
S.S. Adhikari, learned Brief Holder for the State
requested to hear the appeal finally at this stage waiving
requirement of the preparation of the paper book. On
the joint request of the learned counsel for the parties,
requirement of preparation of the paper book was
waived and appeal was taken up for hearing finally.
Present appeal is directed against the judgment
and order dated 02.04.2013 and 04.04.2013 passed by
Additional Sessions Judge Khatima, District Udham
Singh Nagar in Session Trial No. 222 of 2010, whereby
appellant was found guilty for the offences punishable
under Sections 366 and 376 I.P.C. and was sentenced to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of three
years and to pay fine of Rs.500/-, and in default of
making payment of fine, to undergo additional simple
imprisonment of 10 days under Section 366 I.P.C. ; to
undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of seven
years and to pay fine of Rs.500/-, and in default of

2
making payment of fine, to undergo additional simple
imprisonment of 10 days under Section 376 I.P.C. with
the stipulation that both the sentences shall run
concurrently.
Brief facts of the present case, inter alia, are that
PW1 Bhakto Sikandar, father of the prosecutrix lodged
an F.I.R. with the Police Station Sitarganj on 02.07.2010
stating therein that on 26.06.2010 prosecutrix went to
withdraw money from Shakti Farm Post Office,
however, accused took her away by deceitful means with
object to marry her; PW3 Kalyan Halder saw the
appellant in the company of the prosecutirx near
Kushmoth Tirah; on the report of PW1 Bhakto Sikandar
so lodged, Chick F.I.R was registered for the offence
punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376 I.P.C.
Appellant and prosecutrix were apprehended on
03.07.2010 near the Pul Bhatta; prosecutrix was
medically examined by PW7 Dr. Sammi Unissa on
03.07.2010 itself and as per the report she was found
aged about 18 years; statements of the prosecutrix were
also recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 17.07.2010.
Having investigated the matter, Investigating
Officer PW4 S.I. Jitendra Singh Chauhan submitted
chargesheet against the appellant for the offence
punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376 I.P.C. After
committal, learned trial court was pleased to frame
charges against the appellant for the offence punishable
under Section 363, 366 and 376 I.P.C. Appellant denied
the charges and claimed trial.

3
To prove the prosecution story, PW1 father of the
prosecutrix Bhakto Sikandar, PW2 prosecurtix Km.
Meena Sikandar, PW3 Kalyan Haldwar, PW4 S.I.
Jitendra Singh Chauhan, PW5 lady Constable Anita,
PW6 lady Constabale Sivanti Rana and PW7 Dr. Sammi
Unissa were examined. Thereafter, statement of
appellant was also recorded under Section 313 of the
Cr.P.C.
Having perused the entire material made available
on record, learned Trial Judge was pleased to convict
and sentence the appellant vide judgment and order
impugned in the present appeal.
I have heard Mr. S.R.S. Gill, learned counsel for
the appellant and Mr. S.S. Adhikari, learned Brief
Holder for the State and have carefully perused the
record.
As per the statement of proseuctrix PW2, she left
her house on 26.06.2010 to go to Shakti Farm Post
Office for withdrawal of money; appellant met her there;
appellant told the prosecutrix if she wish he could take
her for joy ride; appellant took her to Bareilly on the
pretext of visiting Bareilly; appellant and prosecutrix
stayed in a hotel at Bareilly wherein appellant made
physical relations of husband and wife with the
prosecutrix; prosecutrix stayed in the hotel for seven
days and when appellant brought her back to Pul Bhatta
to drop her, they were apprehended by the police.

4
During the cross examination, prosecutrix stated
that appellant was known to her since her childhood; no
direct bus goes to Bareilly from the Shakti Farm; she
and appellant boarded in the bus which was going to
Kitchha; both of them left that bus at Kichcha Bus
Station; she did not make any noise at Kichha Bus
Station; from Kichha, she went Bareilly on motorcycle
with the appellant; friend of the appellant brought the
motorcycle to go to Bareilly; she did not make any noise
while staying in the hotel room; thereafter appellant
brought her back Pul Bhatta to drop her to her
residence.
I have perused the entire statements of the
prosecutrix, prosecutrix seems to be a consenting party
for the simple reason that prosecutrix agreed to go to
Bareilly with the appellant; both of them boarded bus at
Shakti Farm for Kitchha and from Kitchha both of them
went Bareilly by the Motorcycle; she did not report the
matter to anyone while traveling in the bus or at Kitchha
bus station; she could have resisted while making
entries at the hotel reception for taking room in the
hotel for long seven days; after staying in the hotel for
long seven days she came back with appellant to Pul
Bhatta; prosecutrix was found to be aged about 18 years
by PW7 Dr. Sammi Unissa.
In view of the discussion made hereinabove, in the
firm opinion of this Court, prosecution was not able to
prove the prosecution story beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, conviction of the appellant seems to be

5
totally unjustified. Consequently, present appeal is
allowed. Impugned judgment and order passed by
Additional Sessions Judge Khatima, District Udham
Singh Nagar in Session Trial No. 222 of 2010 is set
aside.
Appellant stands acquitted from the charges
leveled against him. Appellant is in jail. He may be
released forthwith, if not wanted in any other case.
Let copy of the judgment alongwith L.C.R. be sent
back to the lower court for information and compliance
immediately.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
Dated 18th June, 2013 Shiv
